confirm.text: Three air job forms selected "Unsafe conditions" in the OWL "What did we observe?" list. On all three the full multi-select string is byte-for-byte identical, ten items long, and no narrative anywhere on any of the three forms describes an actual unsafe condition, hazard, incident, near miss or equipment problem. Every free-text field on all three is positive or administrative. This matches the mis-selection pattern Kelby described on 09/23 and should be handled as a training item with the technicians, not as three unsafe-condition events.

Worth noting separately: none of the three selected "Stop work authority utilized". All three selected "Stop work authority was discussed", which is a routine pre-job item. No form filed on 09/26 records stop-work authority being used.

Michael Jobe — XTO, Benedum 3D 4H, job 35071_1, 02:22–03:23 PM. Selected "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative: "Had meeting mt went over everything as needed" and "Crew completed work in a safe manner".
Michael Jobe — XTO, Louis 3142, job 35025_1, 08:02 AM–01:23 PM. Same ten-item selection. Narrative: "Had a good meeting went over what needed to be done".

Nathan Contreras — XTO, Morgan Owens 24A 1H, job 35029_1, 07:15–09:28 AM. Same ten-item selection. Narrative: "We observed a disconnect done on a wellhead" and Details "Monitored benzene on wellhead disconnect" — routine scope, not a hazard.

Nathan Contreras has now appeared on this list on more than one day. He was on the stop-work confirmation list as of 09/23 and is on it again here. Michael Jobe appears twice in a single day, on two different jobs, with an identical selection string. That the same ten-item string appears on all three forms suggests the selection is being carried forward rather than made fresh each job, which is worth raising with both men directly.

No form on 09/26 is in the Ralph Forbes or Ruben Rojo category from 09/23 — there is no narrative naming a real condition, and none of the three has an entirely blank close-out that would leave the selection unoffset.

Trailer inspections and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review — I can see that a photo exists and when it was taken, but not what it shows. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, never as text fields, so nothing in this report should be read as confirming that any of those are current.
